packages.area: iOS + Apple Watch App Store readiness (project.yml, assets, Info.plist keys, Swift app/watch sources, docs/store)

items.text: Embedded Apple Watch app has no app icon: App Store Connect upload validation will fail (ITMS-90713) — ios/project.yml:97-125 (BinarioWatch target) lists sources ../apple-watch/BinarioWatch, ../apple-watch/Shared, ../apple-watch/Resources and sets no ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME; `find apple-watch -name '*.xcassets' -o -name '*.png'` returns nothing; apple-watch/project.yml:10-33 likewise. Only the iPhone target has ios/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset (ios/project.yml:48 ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon). A watchOS app bundle without CFBundleIconName/1024 icon is rejected at upload ('Missing Info.plist value ... CFBundleIconName ... in the bundle it.binario.ios.watchkitapp'). The simulator-only CI (CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO, no archive) cannot catch this.
items.fix_summary: Add apple-watch/BinarioWatch/Assets.xcassets/Contents.json ({"info":{"author":"xcode","version":1}}) and apple-watch/BinarioWatch/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/Contents.json with a single image {"filename":"AppIcon-1024.png","idiom":"universal","platform":"watchos","size":"1024x1024"} plus an opaque 1024x1024 RGB PNG (no alpha, no rounded corners; e.g. generated from the same brand source as ios/Resources/Assets.xcassets/AppIcon.appiconset/AppIcon-1024.png by extending tools/build_store_assets.py). Put it under BinarioWatch/ (not Resources/) so the widget target does not carry it. Add `ASSETCATALOG_COMPILER_APPICON_NAME: AppIcon` to BinarioWatch settings.base in BOTH ios/project.yml and apple-watch/project.yml. Extend tests/test_verify_ios_project.py and tests/test_verify_apple_watch_project.py to assert the appiconset exists, Contents.json has platform watchos/size 1024x1024, and the PNG is 1024x1024 colour type 2 or 6 with fully opaque alpha.
items.verification: Static: python3 -I check that Contents.json parses and the PNG header reads 1024x1024 without transparency; python3 -m unittest tests.test_verify_ios_project tests.test_verify_apple_watch_project. Real proof only via xcodebuild archive + App Store validation on macOS.
items.owner_action: None beyond the upload itself; on macOS run `xcodebuild archive` and 'Validate App' in Xcode Organizer to confirm the watch icon is accepted.

items.text: No signing/team configuration is persisted: every regenerated Xcode project is unsigned and the three App IDs + App Group must be re-selected by hand — .gitignore:37 ignores ios/Binario.xcodeproj/, so the project exists only after `xcodegen generate` (ios/Scripts/generate-project.sh). ios/project.yml contains no DEVELOPMENT_TEAM, CODE_SIGN_STYLE or CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY for Binario (lines 37-50), BinarioWatch (112-121) or BinarioWatchWidgets (154-162); ios/APPLE_PLATFORM_READINESS.md:60 confirms 'No signing configuration is checked in'. Archiving for App Store requires a team on all three targets plus the App Groups capability on it.binario.ios.watchkitapp and it.binario.ios.watchkitapp.widgets (apple-watch/BinarioWatch/BinarioWatch.entitlements: group.it.binario.watch).
items.fix_summary: In ios/project.yml settings.base add `CODE_SIGN_STYLE: Automatic` and `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM: ${BINARIO_APPLE_TEAM_ID}` (XcodeGen substitutes environment variables), or add `configFiles: { Release: Signing.xcconfig }` with an untracked ios/Signing.xcconfig and a committed ios/Signing.xcconfig.example; document the variable in ios/Scripts/generate-project.sh and ios/APPLE_PLATFORM_READINESS.md. Keep CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO in CI unchanged.

items.text: ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption missing from all three Info.plists: every uploaded build is held as 'Missing Compliance' — ios/project.yml:37-50 (Binario) and :112-121 (BinarioWatch) generate Info.plist via GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE with no INFOPLIST_KEY_ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption; apple-watch/BinarioWatchWidgets/Info.plist has no ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption key. grep for URLSession/Network/CryptoKit/CommonCrypto/Security in ios/BinarioApp, ios/BinarioKit/Sources and apple-watch returns nothing: the app performs no networking and uses only a pure-Swift SHA-256 for integrity (BundledGTFSScheduleInstaller.swift:225), so the correct answer is NO (exempt). Without the key App Store Connect asks the export-compliance question after each upload and blocks TestFlight until answered.
items.fix_summary: Add `INFOPLIST_KEY_ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: NO` to settings.base of Binario and BinarioWatch in ios/project.yml (Xcode injects every INFOPLIST_KEY_* build setting into the generated plist, as it already does for WKApplication/WKWatchOnly) and `<key>ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption</key><false/>` to apple-watch/BinarioWatchWidgets/Info.plist; mirror in apple-watch/project.yml. Assert the setting in tests/test_verify_ios_project.py (test_app_identity_version_and_swift6_phone_deployment_are_explicit) and the plist key in tests/test_verify_apple_watch_project.py.
items.verification: Static (yaml/plist assertions in the Python tests); on macOS `plutil -p <archive>/Products/Applications/Binario.app/Info.plist | grep ITSApp`.
items.owner_action: None once the key ships (otherwise answer 'No' to 'Does your app use encryption?' in App Store Connect for every build).

items.text: Planner offers 5,239 stations but the bundled timetable serves only 610 (no Trenitalia/Italo): Roma Termini and Napoli Centrale return 'no data' - App Review 2.1/4.2 trap — Decompressing ios/Resources/binario_gtfs_schedule_v1.sqlite.zlib and running `select count(distinct catalog_station_id) from stop join stop_time ...` gives 610 of the 5,239 catalog stations (11.6%). Roma Termini S08409, Napoli Centrale S09218, Venezia Santa Lucia NC001358, Palermo Centrale S12002: 0 stop_times; Torino Porta Nuova: 5 (SNCF only); Bologna Centrale: 3 (SBB only). Packs (metadata.json packRowCounts): STA, ARST, SBB ch-otd, EAV, HZPP (0 trips), Trenord, OeBB, SNCF, TFT, Trentino - no national operator. StationPickerField.swift:265 `model.suggestions(for:)` -> CuratedStationCatalog.search over the whole catalog with no coverage marking; PlannerView.swift:16-19 intro and it.lproj/Localizable.strings `settings.data.provider_programmed` = '10 fonti GTFS incluse · dati programmati' never say which operators are included. A reviewer testing the two most famous Italian stations sees result.unavailable ('Dati non disponibili') and may file 'app does not work' (Guideline 2.1) or minimum functionality (4.2).
items.fix_summary: In SQLiteGTFSJourneyRepository add `coveredCatalogStationIDs() throws -> Set<String>` (SELECT DISTINCT catalog_station_id FROM stop WHERE catalog_station_id IS NOT NULL - 610 rows) executed once in AppModel.loadSchedule and published as `coveredStationIDs`; in StationSearchView show a secondary label (new key e.g. `planner.station.no_timetable` = 'Orari non inclusi') for uncovered stations and sort covered ones first (or filter them when scheduleState == .available); add a planner footer listing the included feeds (read from the bundled binario_gtfs_source_policy_v1.json / SQLite pack table); rewrite `planner.intro.body` and `settings.data.provider_programmed` in all five .lproj files to state that only the listed regional/foreign feeds are included and that Trenitalia/Italo are not. Add a BinarioKit test for coveredCatalogStationIDs against the committed artifact.
items.verification: python3 -I script over the decompressed artifact (kept at scratchpad/store/appstore-ios/gtfs.sqlite) to recount covered stations; `swift test --package-path ios/BinarioKit` on a Swift host; Python localisation parity tests.
items.owner_action: In App Store Connect 'Notes for Review' give a covered test route (e.g. Milano Centrale -> Bergamo, Trenord; Bolzano -> Merano, STA) and state the coverage; write the description honestly ('orari programmati offline di 9 feed GTFS regionali ed esteri; Trenitalia/Italo non inclusi').

No isPaired/isWatchAppInstalled check exists (grep). A reviewer on a plain iPhone sees a red-flag 'update failed'.

items.text: Watch detail shows raw 'PROGRAMMED' status and the headline is red 'Dati non disponibili in tempo reale' for every programmed snapshot — SQLiteGTFSJourneyRepository.swift:335 sets status: OperationalState.programmed.rawValue; AppModel.swift:297 publishes freshness .unknown; WatchHomeView.swift:41-43 colours BinarioFreshness.unknown red with watch.freshness.unavailable, WatchHomeView.swift:126 prints service.status verbatim.
items.fix_summary: Map status/freshness to catalogue keys on the Watch (WatchModels.swift) and publish a freshness value that means 'scheduled' instead of unknown.

items.text: Apple Watch CI never archives a Release build, so the product App Store Connect receives is unverified — .github/workflows/apple-watch-ci.yml: watchos job runs `xcodebuild ... build` / `test` on the standalone project; ios job runs only `xcodebuild -scheme Binario -destination id=<iOS sim> CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO test` (Debug, simulator). No `xcodebuild archive -configuration Release -destination generic/platform=iOS`, no exportArchive, no validation; thus Release optimisation, the generated Info.plists (icons, export-compliance key), embedding of Watch/BinarioWatch.app and PlugIns/BinarioWatchWidgets.appex, and PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy placement are never checked. Latest green run 39152547601 (2026-10-18) confirms only Debug simulator builds/tests.
items.fix_summary: Add a step to the ios job: `xcodebuild archive -project Binario.xcodeproj -scheme Binario -configuration Release -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' -archivePath "$RUNNER_TEMP/Binario.xcarchive" CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` followed by assertions (`plutil -p` CFBundleIconName in Products/Applications/Binario.app/Info.plist and Watch/BinarioWatch.app/Info.plist, ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, existence of PlugIns/BinarioWatchWidgets.appex and of PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy in all three bundles) and `actions/upload-artifact` of the xcarchive; update .github/ci-inputs-lock.json appleIosRunSteps and tools/verify_ci_pinning.py expectations; optionally add the BinarioWatch test run on the integrated project (R4:L-I-4).
items.verification: python3 tools/verify_ci_pinning.py; python3 -m unittest tests.test_verify_ci_pinning; real run needs a GitHub macOS runner.
items.owner_action: For a signed export in CI add App Store Connect API key secrets (ASC_KEY_ID, ASC_ISSUER_ID, ASC_API_KEY_P8) and an ExportOptions.plist (method app-store-connect); otherwise archive and upload from Xcode Organizer on a Mac.

items.text: Standalone apple-watch/project.yml is a Swift 5.10 watch-only app with no data path: fine as a test harness, must never be submitted, and it is the only place the Watch tests run — apple-watch/project.yml:6 SWIFT_VERSION 5.10 vs ios/project.yml:7 SWIFT_VERSION 6.0; :21-22 WKWatchOnly: YES with bundle it.binario.watch; PhoneConnectivity.swift:208-229 only receives WCSession application contexts from an iPhone companion that a watch-only app does not have, so the standalone app can only ever show BinarioWatchSnapshot.unavailable (4.2 minimum functionality if submitted). The CI watchos job is the only job executing BinarioWatchTests (Swift 5 mode); the integrated Swift 6 watch build is compiled but never tested (R4:L-I-4).
items.fix_summary: Set SWIFT_VERSION 6.0 in apple-watch/project.yml (update tests/test_verify_apple_watch_project.py), state in apple-watch/APPLE_WATCH_IMPLEMENTATION.md and README.md that the standalone project is a CI/test harness and that the store product is the embedded target of ios/project.yml, and run `xcodebuild -project Binario.xcodeproj -scheme BinarioWatch -destination id=<watch sim> test` in the ios job.
items.verification: python3 -m unittest tests.test_verify_apple_watch_project; CI run on macOS.
items.owner_action: Do not create an App Store record for it.binario.watch.

items.text: INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDevelopmentRegion / CFBundleLocalizations conflict with XcodeGen's default development language — ios/project.yml:43-44 set INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleDevelopmentRegion: it and INFOPLIST_KEY_CFBundleLocalizations: [it, en, de, fr, es], while options: (lines 2-4) has no developmentLanguage, so XcodeGen writes developmentRegion/knownRegions 'en' and DEVELOPMENT_LANGUAGE=en into the project; CFBundleLocalizations is redundant with the five .lproj folders and, as a list build setting, may not serialise as a plist array.
items.fix_summary: Remove both INFOPLIST_KEY_ entries and set `options.developmentLanguage: it` (fallback for unsupported device languages = Italian, like Android) or `en`; adjust tests/test_verify_ios_project.py accordingly.
items.verification: python3 -m unittest tests.test_verify_ios_project; macOS: `plutil -p Binario.app/Info.plist | grep CFBundle`.

items.text: App will be offered on Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision Pro ('Designed for iPhone') by default, where Watch Connectivity is unsupported and nothing was tested — ios/project.yml:49-50 sets TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY "1" and SUPPORTS_MACCATALYST NO but not SUPPORTS_MAC_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD / SUPPORTS_XR_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD; App Store Connect then lists the iPhone app for Mac and visionOS unless the owner opts out. WCSession.isSupported() is false there (AppModel/WCSessionAdapter handle it as .unsupported) but the UI was never exercised on those platforms.
items.fix_summary: Add `SUPPORTS_MAC_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD: NO` and `SUPPORTS_XR_DESIGNED_FOR_IPHONE_IPAD: NO` to the Binario target settings (or decide to support them and test).
items.owner_action: Alternatively uncheck 'Make this app available on Mac / Apple Vision' in App Store Connect Pricing and Availability.

items.text: Settings hard-codes data identity strings that will drift ('stazioni-ferroviarie-curato-v4', '10 fonti GTFS incluse' while HZPP contributes 0 trips) and two required localisation keys are unused — SettingsView.swift:10 `Text("stazioni-ferroviarie-curato-v4")` literal (resolved as a LocalizedStringKey, not from the loaded catalog's sourceDatabaseName); it/en/de/fr/es `settings.data.provider_programmed` embed the number 10 although metadata.json packRowCounts shows hzpp-gtfs with pack:1 and no trips (9 feeds with data) and the count changes on every refresh. BinarioLocalizationKeys.required contains `app.name` and `planner.route_accessibility` which no view references (grep over ios/BinarioApp).
items.fix_summary: Read CuratedStationCatalog.sourceDatabaseName and the SQLite pack count (packs with trips) in AppModel and format `settings.data.provider_programmed` with a %lld placeholder; drop or use the two unused keys.

items.text: Every launch re-hashes the 24.5 MB timetable with pure-Swift SHA-256 while the planner shows a spinner and disables search — BundledGTFSScheduleInstaller.swift:33-41 fast path calls hashFile(destination) (Array(data) copy + Swift SHA-256, lines 194-287) on each launch; PlannerView.swift:37-43 and :67-69 keep 'Preparazione degli orari programmati…' and the disabled search button until it finishes. Reviewer-visible delay on older iPhones.
items.fix_summary: Trust the stored sha256 + size + fingerprint on the fast path (or hash with CryptoKit off-main only on first install).

suites: Swift: static only — NO compiler here; keep every Swift change minimal, consistent with the existing Swift 6 strict-concurrency code, and double-check types/optionals by reading the surrounding code; the Apple Watch CI workflow on GitHub builds and tests the project after the push, so compile errors would surface there
